findings.title: Paired perceptual refusal
findings.claim: تَوَلَّىٰ turns the hearer away from an orientation already opened by reminder and looking, while كَفَرَ covers the truth that this orientation exposes; the two verbs form a coordinated refusal.
findings.mechanism: The focus B006/B007 opposition supplies the changed direction of face and attention, and the focus B001/B003 opposition supplies concealment or rejection as the response to what has been faced. Strong connections at 53:29, 53:33, 75:32, and 37:170 independently return the turning-plus-covering relation to the focus pair.
findings.reader_payoff: The clause becomes a sequence of redirected attention followed by suppression of what attention could disclose, rather than two detached labels for motion and belief.
findings.containment: The conjunction does not prove causal order; this retains coordinated perceptual refusal without claiming that turning must cause denial or that every occurrence of either root has this sense.

epistemic.reason: The retained cross-run support is trusted and strongly anchored, while the direction from the preceding imagery into this exact clause remains an interpretive relation.

findings.title: Seed-cover counter-image
findings.claim: As a contained ecological counter-image, delayed rain and seed-covering show that hiddenness can precede emergence, making the focus covering a morally perverted use of an operation that can also nurture.

Their continuous ecological chain changes covering from simple suppression into an operation whose latent outcome can be either growth or denial.
findings.reader_payoff: The same visible operation can be understood as enabling emergence or suppressing recognition, sharpening the moral contrast in the focus pair.
findings.containment: This is an exploratory legacy_unbound analogical outlier. It must never be rendered as the lexical meaning of 88:23 or as a claim that moral rejection is generative.

epistemic.reason: The exact trace forms a coherent ecological chain, but both focus branches are form-distant outlier senses and the resulting relation is explicitly analogical.
